newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices off 1/4 to 3/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices off 1/4 to 3/8.

text.p: down 1/4 to 3/8 of a point on Wednesday, traders said.
Overall trading activity was moderate, with about $200 million of bid lists circulating in the market.
High grade municipal bonds rose about two basis points, erasing midday gains, while dollar bonds were off 3/8 of a point overall.
Maryland's $170 million general obligation bond issue was the highlight of the day, although the triple-A rated offering did get caught in the market downdraft.
Smith Barney Inc, which won the competitive offering at 1100 EDT with a 4.97 percent true interest cost, reported an unsold balance of around $95 million at 1500 EDT.
A municipal market analyst said the issue was priced "at the right price to buy Maryland. The problem was the market walked away from them."
Maryland is the "consistent premier bond and it was priced like that," the analyst said. But the drop in the U.S. Treasury market hurt the issue.
"If it had been priced at (1400 EDT) it would have been an 05 cheaper," the analyst said. "It was market risk."
As for follow through, the analyst suggested he would wait until Friday before trying to move any of the Maryland GOs.
"I would not go out looking for down business," he said. "I have a feeling, unless there is extraordinary news, everything waits until Friday and the PPI (Producer Prices Index) release."
The Treasury long bond closed down 10 basis points to yield 6.83 percent.
